The kitchen sink was full of dishes.
Water ran from the faucet into the sink.

easy.def: To go down below the water.
examples: The rock sinks.
The boat sank.
Stones sink in water.

more.def: To go down below the surface of water or another liquid.
examples: The heavy rock sank to the bottom of the pond.
The boat began to sink.
Metal coins sink in water.

easy.def: A small weight on a fishing line.
examples: A sinker is on the line.
The sinker is heavy.
He added a sinker.

more.def: A small weight attached to a fishing line to make it sink.
examples: He added a sinker to the fishing line.
The sinker pulled the hook down.
A small lead sinker sank to the bottom.

easy.def: A big hole that opens up in the ground.
examples: A sinkhole opened.
The sinkhole was deep.
Cars avoid the sinkhole.

more.def: A large hole that suddenly opens in the ground when the earth underneath washes away.
examples: A sinkhole opened in the middle of the road.
Rain can cause a sinkhole to form.
A fence was put around the sinkhole.

easy.def: An air space inside your head, near your nose.
examples: I have a stuffy sinus.
The sinus hurts.
Your sinuses are in your head.

more.def: One of the empty spaces in the bones of your face and head that are connected to your nose.
examples: When I have a cold, my sinuses fill up and my nose gets stuffy.
The doctor said the pain above my eyes was in my sinuses.
Your sinuses help make your voice sound the way it does.

easy.def: To drink in small amounts.
examples: I sip my juice.
She sipped her tea.
He sipped the hot soup.

more.def: To drink slowly, taking a little at a time.
examples: I sipped my hot chocolate slowly.
She sipped the tea carefully.
He sipped from the water bottle.

easy.def: A polite word used to speak to a man.
examples: Yes, sir.
Excuse me, sir.
Thank you, sir.

more.def: A polite word used when speaking to a man, especially one you do not know or one who is older.
examples: Excuse me, sir, you dropped your hat.
Yes, sir, I will be there at noon.
Can I help you carry that, sir?

easy.def: A loud alarm that wails.
examples: The siren blared.
The fire truck has a siren.
I heard a siren.

more.def: A device that makes a loud, long sound to warn people.
examples: The ambulance siren wailed down the street.
A siren warned us of the storm.
The police car turned on its siren.

easy.def: A girl who has the same parents as you.
examples: My sister is tall.
I play with my sister.
Her sister is six.

more.def: A girl or woman who has the same parents as another person.
examples: My older sister helps me with my reading.
He has two sisters, and they love to bake.
Her little sister follows her around the yard.

easy.def: Being like sisters, or a group of women who feel close.
examples: The sisterhood is strong.
They share a sisterhood.
A sisterhood of friends.

more.def: The bond between sisters, or a group of women who feel close and support each other.
examples: The club is a sisterhood of friends.
The girls felt a sisterhood.
The sisterhood helped one another.

easy.def: To rest with your bottom on a seat or the ground.
examples: Sit on the chair.
The cat sat on my lap.
We sit in a circle.

more.def: To rest with your weight on your bottom, rather than on your feet.
examples: Please sit quietly on the rug while I read.
The birds sat on the wire, side by side.
We sat around the campfire and sang songs.

easy.def: A funny TV show about a family or friends.
examples: We watched a sitcom.
The sitcom was funny.
A sitcom about a family.

more.def: A funny television show about the same characters in different everyday situations each week; short for situation comedy.
examples: We laughed at the sitcom about a family with a talking dog.
A sitcom is a funny show about everyday life.
My favorite sitcom is on every Tuesday.

easy.def: A place where something is or will be.
examples: We visited a building site.
This is a good site for a tent.
The site is a park.

more.def: The place where something happens or is built.
examples: The workers cleaned the building site.
The campers chose a flat site by the stream.
The old castle is a famous historic site.

easy.def: A person who looks after kids or pets while parents are away.
examples: The sitter came.
Our sitter is kind.
The sitter read us a story.

more.def: A person who takes care of children or pets for a short time while the parents or owners are away.
examples: Our sitter came over and played games with us while Mom was at work.
The sitter gave the dog dinner.
A pet sitter looked after the cat while we were on vacation.

easy.def: The way things are at a certain time.
examples: We are in a tricky situation.
The situation is better now.
What a funny situation!

more.def: The set of things that are happening around you at a certain time.
examples: We were in a difficult situation when the bus broke down.
The teacher explained the situation to the class.
Staying calm helps in any situation.

easy.def: The number after five.
examples: I have six crayons.
An insect has six legs.
We eat dinner at six.

more.def: The number 6, which comes after five and before seven.
examples: A cube has six faces, one on each side.
The bus leaves at six o'clock every morning.
She scored six points in the basketball game.

easy.def: The number 16.
examples: I am sixteen.
There are sixteen crayons.
Sixteen kids came.

more.def: The number that comes after fifteen, written 16.
examples: My cousin is sixteen years old.
There are sixteen ounces in a pound.
The team has sixteen players.

easy.def: Number 16 in a row.
examples: It was her sixteenth birthday.
He was sixteenth.
The sixteenth page.

more.def: Coming after the fifteenth and before the seventeenth.
examples: My sister will have her sixteenth birthday next week.
He finished in sixteenth place.
The sixteenth chapter was the best.

easy.def: Number six in a line.
examples: I am sixth in line.
She came in sixth.
It is the sixth day.

more.def: Coming after the fifth one and before the seventh one.
examples: He finished sixth in the race.
My sister is in sixth grade.
The sixth chapter is the longest.

easy.def: One of six equal parts.
examples: I ate a sixth of the pizza.
A sixth is a small part.
Cut it in sixths.

more.def: One of six equal parts that make a whole.
examples: Each of us got a sixth of the pie.
A sixth of the class is absent.
Add a sixth of a cup of milk.

easy.def: The number 60.
examples: There are sixty minutes in an hour.
I counted to sixty.
The pool is sixty feet long.

more.def: The number that comes after fifty-nine, written 60.
examples: A minute has sixty seconds.
I counted to sixty by tens.
The bus holds sixty students.

easy.def: Fairly large.
examples: A sizable crowd.
The cake is sizable.
We have a sizable yard.

more.def: Fairly large in size or amount.
examples: A sizable crowd came to the fair.
The cake was sizable, with room for twenty slices.
They have a sizable collection of toys.

easy.def: How big or small something is.
examples: The size of the box is big.
What size are your shoes?
The dogs are all different sizes.

more.def: How large something is, or the amount of space it takes up.
examples: The elephant is an animal of great size.
What size shoes do you wear?
Boxes come in many sizes.

easy.def: To make a hissing sound when cooking.
examples: The bacon sizzled.
The pan sizzles.
Sausages sizzle on the grill.

more.def: To make a hissing, crackling sound, as food does when it is cooking in hot fat.
examples: The bacon sizzled in the hot pan.
The sausages sizzled on the grill.
Water sizzled when it hit the hot stove.
